2. Facts, for disposal of the appeal in short are that the appellant as plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 54 of 2001 before the Court of Assistant Judge, Tarash, Sirajganj for declaration of title of 2.27 acres of land and further declaration that the Deed No. 8999 dated 24.11.1969 of Naogaon Sub-Registry Office was forged, collusive not acted upon and not binding upon the plaintiff. The case of the plaintiff, inter alia was that 3.06 acres land of C.S Plot No. 403 in C.S. Khatian No. 41 under Sree Krishnapur Mouza originally belonged to Brindaban Goshwami and the land was recorded in his name as pond, that Brindaban Goshwami was a Brahman priest and he used to live in another village namely Handial under Chatmohar Police Station of Pabna District and possessed the same through a caretaker named Sree Badal; that in addition said Brindaban Goshwami occasionally used to live at the home constructed in the eastern part of the pond for maintaining the property and the S.A khatian No.61 was prepared his name correctly in respect of said property; that Brindaban Goshwami had no child and because of inconvenience in managing the pond due to short-age of manpower he kept .38 acres of land in eastern part of the pond whereupon a but was built under his own management and sold the remaining 2.68 acres to the plaintiff by a registered sale deed No.11727 dated 19.09.1979 corresponding to 2nd Aswin, 1386 B.S; that after purchase, the plaintiff had been possessing the purchased land and entered his name in R.S khatian No.397 and converted plot No.473 but when the plaintiff submitted the original sale deed to the Tahshilder, the concerned Tahshilder lost it; that the plain-tiff obtained the finally published corrected R.S record; that in the meantime the defendant in collusion with the custodians of R.S record volume managed to enter his name in printed parcha in place of plain-tiff s name in R.S khatian No.397 which is illegal; that for extension of periphery of Sree Krishnapur Hat as per demand by the committee, the plaintiff transferred .41 acre out of the suit land in favour of Hat Committee and the plaintiff had been possessing remaining 2.27 acres of land peacefully by rearing of fishes and planting different trees in the southern part of the suit land; that while the plaintiff was possessing the remaining 2.27 acres of land, all of a sudden he received notice of Miscellaneous Case No.80 of 2001 from the office of Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tarash and on 29.04.2001 he searched the office and came to know about the existence of deed No.8999 dated 24.11.1969 of Naogaon Sub-Registry office in respect of Suit land which is a product of collusive acts. Hence, He filed the suit. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material facts and averments made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Brindaban Goshwami sold 1.90 acres of land from Plot No.403 by a registered deed of sale No.8999 dated 24.11.1969 and accordingly his name was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 397; that 2.68 acres out of 3.06 in C.S and R.S Plot No.403 was recorded in R.S Plot No.473 and remaining .38 acres was recorded in R.S. Plot No. 474 and the defendant purchased .38 acre of land from Badal Chandra Bashak but got entire 3.06 acres of land; that the defendant transferred .40 acre of land from Northern part in favour of Sree Krishnapur hat commit-tee and the defendant is possessing the remaining 2.66 acres of land; that the owner of the land died in the year of 1972-73 and the plaintiff has no right title and possession even then he filed this suit with created documents and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Shorif Uddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that both the courts below having seen the original deed dated 24.11.1969 (Ext, la') which had been filed by the defendant, came to a finding that the deed had been created later on and in order to show that it was an old document some mechanism like burning and use of hot vapour was applied upon the document. But such finding of the Courts below that the deed was forged was not controverted by the High Court Division thereby erroneously reversed the concurrent findings of the courts below. The learned counsel further submits that both the Courts below found Exts. 1,2,3 and 4 to be genuine which demonstrated the plaintiffs title and possession of the suit land, but the High Court Division erroneously did not consider these exhibits. Next he submits that the High Court Division failed to consider the observation of the appellate Court that the trial Court had noted the forgery made by the defendant in the register of the suit R.S khatian in connivance with the collectorate staff, but the defendant did not challenge that finding in his appeal. The learned counsel finaily submits that the High Court Division did not properly consider the oral evidence concerning the death of Brindaban Goswami and thereby came to an erroneous finding that the deed of the plaintiff was created after the death of Brindaban Goswami and was not there-fore a genuine one. 

 10. On perusal of Ext. Nos. 2, 3, 4 and 7 it appears that on the basis of the sale deed (Ext. 1) the plaintiff got her name mutated, recorded her name in R.S Khatian and has been paying rents for the suit land. Although the defendant tried to prove by producing 3 Bengali calendars (Ponjeeka) that the plaintiff got the kabala Ext. 1, after the death of Brindabon Goshwami but nowhere in those calendars the name of the father of Brindabon Chandra Goshwami Maharaja has been mentioned. And further it appears that he died at choto Bazar, Mymensingh. This aspect contradicts since from the deposition of defendant DW-1 Ensab Ali who is the main defendant, in the case it appears that Brindabon died in the district of Tangail. Therefore, it is evident that the person shown in the 3 Bangali calendars (Ponjeeka) submitted by the defendant is not the Brindabon Gohswami of the present case. 

 "I have closely perused the kabala of the defendant appellant, Ext. ka, and found it to be artificially old. Such artificiality gets support in the depositions of D.W. 1 Ensab Ali, the defendant, when he states in cross examination that he burnt the kabala when he tried to dry it after getting it wet. The court below rightly held that had the kabala, Ext. Ka got wet then definitely it would have been smudged with its ink. The alleged signatures of the sub-register shown in Ext. ka also do not found to be identical with each other. Finally the court below has disclosed unbelievable forgery made the defendant appellant in the register of the suit R.S Khatian in connivance with the collectorate staff whereagainst the defendant appellant has shown no grievance in the appeal."
